scope.paper_mechanism: GP-UCB transfers information across constrained allocations through kernels; the paper compares noise-free cumulative regret under several changing reward landscapes.
scope.miniature_comparison: 52-round, three-segment simulation comparing independently tuned composite-kernel GP-UCB with epsilon-greedy; RBF GP is an additional arm.
preserved_assumptions: Common initial landscapes and observation-noise stream within seed and context.
Neighbor-constrained allocation moves and delayed observations.
Regret uses the instantaneous noise-free oracle reward.
simplifications: Only three algorithm arms and three environment types; no production deployment.
Steepness and width distributions differ from the source setup.
Separate four-seed hyperparameter search replaces the paper schedules.
unsupported_claims: Reproduction of paper effect sizes or business returns.
Universal GP superiority or policy-independent realized paths in reactive contexts.

evidence.finding: Source parameter draws and exploration schedules need comparison with the miniature.
Steepness uses Uniform(-0.5,1) and widths Uniform(0.05,0.25); source setup uses Uniform(0,1) and Uniform(0,0.1).
Both methods select hyperparameters on four training seeds before final evaluation. This is a different comparison, requiring an explicit scope decision.
Both policies have the same horizon and observation delay, but acquisition and computation differ.
Separate searches use the same training seeds. Equal seed counts do not establish equal tuning effort or comparable cold/warm timing.
Data and action generators are separated; landscape and observation noise are generated before method-specific actions.
Reactive rewards depend on the current action. Shared exogenous randomness does not imply identical realized landscapes under different policies.
Evaluation compares expected rewards to a time-specific oracle.
Cumulative noise-free regret is lower-better. Tuning seed IDs 10001-10004 are separate from cached qualification IDs 4-15.
Tuning seed IDs 10001-10004 are declared here, disjoint from the cached qualification seeds 4-15.
0.3 cumulative-regret units over 52 rounds is about 0.00577 per round. The unit conversion is descriptive; a practical threshold rationale remains unsigned.
Tuning is lru-cached. Repeated-process and fresh-worker behavior and timing need probes; no executions were performed for this draft.
The action-dependent reactive update is intentional feedback, requiring an explicit comparison scope.
Disjoint tuning seeds are reassuring, but broadened landscape parameters and tuning choices could materially change which algorithm wins.
